rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads يؤخره with yāʾ, while the others use nūn; the yāʾ refers to أخذ ربك, whereas nūn begins a new clause, with the same sense.
rows.anchor: قرأ يعقوب وما يؤخره بالياء والباقون بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading refers back to أخذ ربك; the nūn reading begins independently, but has the same meaning.
rows.anchor: من قرأ يؤخره بالياء فإنه رده إلى قوله أخذ ربك

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأهل عرفة غير الكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and the readers of ʿArafa except al-Kisāʾī omit the final yāʾ in يأت; the remaining readers retain it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يوم يأت بغير ياء ابن عامر وأهل عرفة غير الكسائي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj prefers the grammarians’ form يوم يأتي; Hudhayl often delete these yāʾs.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: الذي يختاره النحويون يوم يأتي

rows.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
rows.claim: Sibawayh and al-Khalīl report that Arabs delete the yāʾ in لا أدر through frequent use.
rows.anchor: حكى سيبويه والخليل أن العرب تقول لا أدر

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says retaining yāʾ in connection and pause is the clear regular form; deletion at pause analogizes it to omitted inflection, while deletion in both positions treats it like established irregular forms.
rows.anchor: من أثبت الياء في الوصل والوقف فهو القياس البين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic line deletes the yāʾ of تعطي even though nothing requires deletion.
rows.anchor: كفاك كف لا تبقي درهما

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر
rows.claim: Kūfan readers except Abū Bakr read سعدوا with ḍamma on the sīn; the rest read it with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر سعدوا بضم السين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī finds the ḍamma puzzling because سعد يسعد is intransitive like شقي; an exceptional dialect or paired intransitive/transitive pattern might explain it, while مسعود is not decisive evidence.
rows.anchor: حكى سيبويه سعد يسعد سعادة فهو سعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited لواقح is understood as ملاقح with an augment omitted; by analogy مسعود could derive from أسعد with its augment removed.
rows.anchor: يعني: ملاقح فجاء على حذف الزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetic example يخرجن من أجواز ليل غاضي means مغض and illustrates deletion of an augment.
rows.anchor: ومن الحذف قول الشاعر: يخرجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شقاء, شقاوة, and شقوة mean the same; the yāʾ in شقي comes from wāw, and saʿāda is the opposite of misery.
rows.anchor: الشقاء والشقاوة والشقوة بمعنى والياء في شقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafīr is the beginning of a donkey’s bray and breath repeatedly sounded from grief until the ribs swell; related usage also conveys intensity, burden, mastery, or the sound of fire.
rows.anchor: والزفير أول نهاق الحمار والشهيق آخر نهاقه قال رؤبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafīr is breath repeated with sound from grief until the ribs swell.
rows.anchor: والزفير ترديد النفس مع الصوت من الحزن حتى تنتفخ الضلوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahīq is the dreadful sound drawn from the innermost body with a prolonged breath; its root suggests excessive height or length.
rows.anchor: والشهيق صوت فظيع يخرج من الجوف بمد النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khulūd and dawām both mean everlasting continuance; God is described as دائم but not as خالد.
rows.anchor: والخلود الكون في الأمر أبدا والدوام البقاء أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jadh means cutting off; the author gives Arabic usages including جذه and جذ الله دابرهم.
rows.anchor: والجذ القطع يقال جذه يجذه وجذ الله دابرهم

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s poetic use of تجذ illustrates cutting or severing.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة: تجذ السلوقي المضاعف نسجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day cannot be the subject pronoun of يأتي when it is itself governed by that verb; making the day definite through its own pronoun is rejected.
rows.anchor: فلا يجوز أن يكون فاعله ضمير اليوم

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان المازني
rows.claim: A clause definite through a pronoun cannot be annexed to an adverb; adding tanwīn removes the annexation and makes the construction permissible.
rows.anchor: فإن نونت فقلت آتيك يوما ضحوته باردة أو ليلة أولها مطير جاز لأنه خرج بالتنوين عن حد الإضافة وهذا قول أبي عثمان المازني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day that comes is the Day of Judgment already mentioned in 11:103; يوم means a period or span, not daylight.
rows.anchor: أي يوم يأتي هذا اليوم الذي تقدم ذكره لا تكلم نفس

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows لا تكلم نفس to be a circumstantial clause describing the subject of يأتي or an adjective describing يوم; either analysis requires an understood فيه or deleted object pronoun.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هذه الجملة حالا من الضمير في يأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stronger parse makes يوم يأتي an adverb governed directly by لا تكلم; this avoids the ellipsis required by alternatives, and time nouns naturally attach to verbs.
rows.anchor: وأقول إن الأظهر أن قوله { يوم يأتي } ظرف لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا تكلم means لا تتكلم, with one of the two tāʾs elided, as in the cited poetic example.
rows.anchor: وقوله { لا تكلم } أي لا تتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عطاء is accusative by an implied verb indicated by context: the sense is “He gave them a gift of bliss.”
rows.anchor: وعطاء منصوب بما دل الكلام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God delays the Day only to a counted term because continued obligation benefits creatures until then; the counted limit signals that the Day is near.
rows.anchor: وما نؤخر هذا اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording لأجل signals a wise purpose for delaying the Day, whereas إلى أجل would not express that purpose.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال { لأجل } ولم يقل إلى أجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day’s arrival is the coming of resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: أي حين يأتي القيامة والجزاء

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says no one speaks except with God’s permission and command; people are compelled to leave sins, so only permitted good speech occurs.
rows.anchor: فلا يقع منهم فعل القبيح وأما ما هو غير قبيح فإنه مأذون فيه عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more apparent meaning is that no useful speech, such as intercession or mediation, occurs in the Hereafter except by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن يقال: معناه أنه لا يتكلم أحد في الآخرة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reconciles differing statements by saying the Resurrection has stations: speech is permitted at some and forbidden at others.
rows.anchor: في بعض تلك المواقف ولم يؤذن لهم في الكلام في بعضها عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes “no speech” to mean no speech that supplies an argument: sinners may confess, blame one another, and shift guilt, yet such empty talk counts as no speech.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن معنى قوله { لا ينطقون } أنهم لا ينطقون لحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling people deaf, dumb, and blind explains that argumentless speech counts as no speech: although they hear, speak, and see, they do not accept or consider truth.
rows.anchor: وهم كانوا يسمعون ويتكلمون ويبصرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not being asked about sin means no inquiry to discover what God already knows; questioning instead serves rebuke, reproach, and proof, as in 37:24.
rows.anchor: فمعناه أنهم لا يسألون عن ذنوبهم للتعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People divide into those deserving punishment and reward: the wretched through disobedience, the happy through obedience; misery and happiness are strength of causes of harm and blessing.
rows.anchor: إخبار منه سبحانه بأنهم قسمان أشقياء وهم المستحقون للعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun منهم may refer to the people gathered on the Day in 11:103, or to نفس in this verse, since نفس is generic.
rows.anchor: يعود إلى الناس في قوله { ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched are in the Fire as punishment for evil deeds; they are called wretched before entry because their present state leads to it.
rows.anchor: يعني أن الذين شقوا باستحقاقهم العذاب

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s saying “the wretched one is wretched in his mother’s womb” means the person is known to become wretched through evil deeds leading to Hell, like an old father’s son called an orphan because he will be orphaned.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says these are sounds of distressed, grieving people: zafīr is a harsh beginning of a groan and shahīq a very loud, intense groan like the end of a donkey’s bray.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: الزفير والشهيق من أصوات المكروبين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the sounds as remorse, a high breath, and unceasing weeping.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال: يريد ندامة ونفسا عاليا

rows.speaker: الضحاك والجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Jubbāʾī take this literally of the transformed skies and earth of the Hereafter, which will not perish when recreated after annihilation.
rows.anchor: أن المراد ما دامت السماوات والأرض مبدلتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view means the skies and earth of Paradise and Hell: everything above is sky and everything under one’s feet is earth; this is close to the first view.
rows.anchor: أن المراد ما دامت سماوات الجنة والنار وأرضهما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the phrase means the Hereafter, which lasts forever, just as the world’s skies and earth endured for the duration of its construction.
rows.anchor: وهي دائمة أبدا كما أن دوام السماء والأرض في الدنيا قدر مدة بنائها عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an Arabic idiom of perpetuity, not a literal time limit: formulas about night and day, sky and earth, and other supposedly unchanging things mean forever.
rows.anchor: ألفاظا للتبعيد في معنى التأبيد يقولون لا أفعل ذلك ما اختلف الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
rows.claim: Poetry by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib uses the two unsetting stars as an image of enduring permanence; Zuhayr similarly speaks of mountains, sky, stars, and lasting days.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو بن معد يكرب:

rows.speaker: الزجاج والفراء وعلي بن عيسى
rows.claim: One view makes the exception an increase beyond the stated span: extra punishment for Hell’s people or bliss for Paradise’s; here إلا means سوى, “apart from.”
rows.anchor: أنه استثناء في الزيادة من العذاب لأهل النار

rows.speaker: المازني والبلخي
rows.claim: Another view applies the exception to time spent at the gathering and judgment or in the barzakh; al-Balkhī prefers this explanation.
rows.anchor: أن الاستثناء واقع على مقامهم في المحشر والحساب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the Hell exception attaches to kinds of torment beyond the two sounds, and the Paradise exception to kinds of bliss; neither limits eternal duration.
rows.anchor: أن الاستثناء الأول يتصل بقوله { لهم فيها زفير وشهيق }

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes إلا to mean “and,” adding whatever God wills; grammarians versed in the language weakened this analysis.
rows.anchor: أن يكون إلا بمعنى الواو أي وما شاء ربك من الزيادة عن الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem describes a vanished house whose remaining cold ashes are guarded from wind; al-Farrāʾ reads إلا there as “and.”
rows.anchor: دان لم يدرس لها رسم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو سعيد الخدري وقتادة والسدي والضحاك
rows.claim: This view says monotheist sinners may be punished in Hell and then taken to Paradise by God’s favor; in the Paradise verse the exception is their time in Hell before transfer. ما may mean من for those removed.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبي سعيد الخدري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this view ما may mean من, referring to the monotheists whom God removes; the author cites Quranic examples and an Arabic expression.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون ما بمعنى من قال سبحانه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says none of these wretched people is an unbeliever: sinful monotheists enter Hell and then God graciously brings them to Paradise, changing their state from wretched to happy.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال الذين شقوا ليس فيهم كافر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says some sinners are scorched by the Fire, then enter Paradise through mercy and intercession; they are called Jahannamiyyūn after the threat is carried out.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة الله أعلم بمشيئته ذكر لنا أن ناسا يصيبهم سفع

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas ibn Mālik reports that the Prophet said a group will come out of the Fire.
rows.anchor: وحدثنا أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda cautions against the Harūriyya position in the context of people being brought out of Hell.
rows.anchor: ولا تقول ما يقوله أهل حروراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author selects the interpretation that sinful monotheists may be released from Hell and brought to Paradise, with a corresponding time exception in the Paradise verse.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول هو المختار المعول عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats the exception as reinforcing eternal punishment: God does not will the release of those whom He has judged to remain.
rows.anchor: أن تعليق ذلك بالمشيئة على سبيل التأكيد للخلود

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God first made an exception and then affirmed His intent in 11:107, “Your Lord does what He wills.”
rows.anchor: ما قاله الحسن أن الله سبحانه استثنى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj and others compare the exception to an oath promising to strike Zayd unless the speaker sees otherwise, though the speaker is resolved to do it.
rows.anchor: قريب منه ما قاله الزجاج وغيره أنه استثناء تستثنيه العرب

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام البصري
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Sallām says the exception refers to earlier groups who entered Hell before later groups, leaving a time gap; he cites 39:71.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى بن سلام البصري

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reports a view from some of his companions that unbelievers are punished in their graves until the world ends, then punishment pauses until resurrection; the exception covers the later interval.
rows.anchor: أورده الشيخ أبو جعفر قدس الله روحه

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abū Mujliz says God may pardon some and spare them entry into Hell; here the exception is of persons.
rows.anchor: أن يتجاوز عنهم فلا يدخلهم النار والاستثناء لأهل التوحيد عن أبي مجلز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those made happy through obedience to God and desisting from sins will be in Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي سعدوا بطاعة الله وانتهائهم عن المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All proposed exception readings for Hell apply here except release of sinners from the Fire after entry: those deserving reward enter Paradise and do not leave it.
rows.anchor: يتأتى فيه جميع ما ذكرنا في الاستثناء من الخلود في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عطاء غير مجذوذ means a gift that is never cut off.
rows.anchor: عطاء غير مجذوذ } أي غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion cites 10:44, “God does not wrong people at all,” in explaining why God does not destroy a community whose members reform.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says God does not punish an individual’s wrongdoing while most people reform, but punishes when corruption and injustice become widespread.
rows.anchor: وثانيها: أن معناه لا يؤاخذهم بظلم واحدهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission, says God does not destroy people for shirk and self-wrongdoing while they deal justly among themselves.
rows.anchor: وثالثها: أنه لا يهلكهم بشركهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in ʿAṭāʾ’s report, parses the wāw in وأهلها as a circumstantial wāw.
rows.anchor: الواو { وأهلها } واو الحال

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet describes the community as reforming and its people as dealing justly with one another.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

words: فَلَوْلَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the account of destroyed nations: they brought ruin on themselves; God would have spared them if believers had enjoined reform and forbidden corruption, but widespread disbelief merited total destruction.
rows.anchor: وجه اتصال قوله تعالى { فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم } الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because سواء is commonly used, it behaves like an active participle; it may also be nominative as though in the position of مستو.
rows.anchor: أي ذات إقبال وإدبار وهذا مما كثر استعماله أعني سواء

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh rejects starting with an indefinite active participle, so he would not allow مستو زيد وعمرو.
rows.anchor: إلا أن سيبويه يستقبح ذلك لا يجيز مستو زيد وعمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what every pregnant female carries, whether male or female, fully formed or not, as well as its color and qualities.
rows.anchor: أي يعلم ما في بطن كل حامل من ذكر أو أنثى

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take wombs’ decrease and increase as shortening or extending the usual nine-month gestation.
rows.anchor: أي يعلم الوقت الذي تنقصه الأرحام من المدة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains decrease and increase as a shorter or longer gestational term, since women do not all give birth at one fixed time.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: الغيض النقصان من الأجل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says decrease is a child born before six months and increase is one born at the maximum gestational duration.
rows.anchor: لأقل من ستة أشهر وما تزداد الولد الذي تأتي به المرأة لأقصى مدة الحمل عن الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in a report through Khilāf, and Ibn Zayd take decrease as cessation of menstrual blood and increase as postpartum blood after birth.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس بخلاف وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything—provision, lifespan, or the pregnancy just mentioned—is measured precisely by God’s wisdom, with neither excess nor deficiency.
rows.anchor: أي وكل شيء من الرزق أو الأجل أو ما سبق ذكره من الحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean knowledge of what is beyond people’s senses and what they witness, or of the nonexistent and existent; al-Ḥasan also glosses it as secret and public.
rows.anchor: أي عالم بما غاب عن حس العباد وبما يشاهده العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a general sense covering every object of knowledge, existent or nonexistent.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن يحمل على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kabīr may mean the master, king, and one able to do all things; alternatively, everything is beneath Him due to perfect attributes, or He is beyond resemblance to creatures.
rows.anchor: وهو السيد الملك القادر على جميع الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutaʿālī is exalted over all by power and has no equal; He is transcendent above what is impermissible in His essence or acts and what polytheists claim.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي علا كل شيء بقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who conceal or voice speech, hide by night, or travel openly by day are alike before God and His knowledge.
rows.anchor: معناه سواء عند الله وفي علمه من أسر القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مستخف is one concealed at night; سارب is someone moving along his route and going about his needs by day.
rows.anchor: ومن هو مستتر متوار بالليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sārib is one traveling his route and pursuing his needs by day.
rows.anchor: ومن هو سالك في سربه أي في مذهبه ماض في حوائجه بالنهار

rows.speaker: مدني شامي والباقون
rows.claim: The Medinan and Syrian readers recite الله الذي in the nominative; the others read it in the genitive.
rows.anchor: الله الذي بالرفع مدني شامي والباقون بالجر

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the genitive reading makes الله an appositive to الحميد, not an adjective; the original إله is a verbal noun meaning the one to whom worship is due.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي بالجر جعله بدلا من الحميد

rows.speaker: أبو زيد ورؤبة
rows.claim: Abū Zayd defines تأله as devotional worship; a rajaz line by Ruʾba uses تألهي as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وأنشد لرؤبة: سبحن واسترجعن من تألهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Allah became dominant through frequent use and functions as a proper name, as descriptive words can become names.
rows.anchor: إلا أن هذا الاسم غلب حتى صار في الغلبة لكثرة استعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example نابغة الجعدي illustrates that an originally descriptive word can become a name and lose its article like Zayd and Jaʿfar.
rows.anchor: والأصل النابغة ولما غلب نزع منه الألف واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nominative الله, the phrase is detached from the previous construction: الذي may be predicate or adjective with an elided predicate; the author compares 34:3.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالرفع قطعه من الأول وجعل الذي الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive reading can make الغيب an adjective of the preceding noun; likewise, in 36:52 هذا may modify مرقدنا or begin a clause with ما وعد الرحمن as predicate.
rows.anchor: ومن جر أجرى الغيب صفة على الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is able to do all things and invulnerable by His power; al-Ḥamīd is praised in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: العزيز القادر على الأشياء الممتنع بقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiḥbāb is seeking to gain love; love can mean willing benefits for the beloved or natural inclination, desire, or appetite, while بغية and ابتغاء mean seeking.
rows.anchor: والاستحباب طلب محبة الشيء بالتعرض لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author directs readers to his earlier discussion in the opening of al-Baqara for meanings and disagreements about the disjoined letters.
rows.anchor: قد ذكرنا معاني الحروف المقطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Qurʾān, brought from God by Gabriel to Muhammad; it is neither sorcery nor poetry.
rows.anchor: نزل به جبرائيل ع من عند الله تعالى

words: لِتُخْرِجَ ٱلنَّاسَ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is sent so that all people may be led from misguidance and disbelief to guidance and faith, by God’s authorization and command.
rows.anchor: من الضلالة إلى الهدى ومن الكفر إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose-marking lām shows that God wills faith for all accountable people; it cannot be a lām of consequence, since that would imply everyone became a believer.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه سبحانه يريد الإيمان من جميع المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light leads to God’s path and knowledge of Him; He is invincible in sovereignty and praised for His acts and blessings to servants.
rows.anchor: أي يخرجهم من ظلمات الكفر إلى طريق الله المؤدي إلى معرفة الله

words: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَهُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns everything in the heavens and earth and has unchallengeable control over it.
rows.anchor: أي له التصرف فيهما على وجه لا اعتراض عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers who deny God’s favors and oneness face woe and severe torment whose pains multiply.
rows.anchor: أخبر أن الويل للكافرين الذين يجحدون نعم الله
